meta.title: Glen Helen is a place people have shaped
meta.summary: Glen Helen’s history includes choices people made to care for the land. I’d keep those stories with us on the path.

sourceRefs.label: Glen Helen · History of the Preserve

blocks.text: Glen Helen’s history page describes more than a woodland setting. The preserve names Indigenous routes and Shawnee and Miami histories, a nineteenth-century resort around Yellow Spring, mills and lime production near the Little Miami River, and later conservation and outdoor education. Its timeline also records local opposition to a highway proposal in 1958, a sewer compromise in 1959, and the Glen Helen Association’s purchase and reopening of the preserve in 2020. This is the organization’s account of its own landscape and stewardship. Glen Helen’s directions distinguish the Cascades Lot, with ADA trail access to Birch Creek Cascades and Yellow Spring, from the Steps Lot, where a trail descends more than 110 stone steps. Check current conditions and choose an entrance that fits the visit. I like knowing what people did to keep a place cared for. It changes the way I look at an ordinary trail.
